capabilities.audience: AI coding agents and automation tools that need to discover how to use exodusii without loading the full documentation corpus.

format.query_language: Lightweight path syntax: whole object with '.', dotted object keys, bracketed object keys, and list indexes. This is not jq.
format.progressive_disclosure: Top-level objects are compact indexes. Query deeper paths for operational details.

overview.what_is_exodusii: exodusii is a Python interface for reading, writing, comparing, querying, and inspecting Sandia Exodus II finite-element databases stored as NetCDF files.
core_use_cases: Inspect mesh and result metadata from finite-element simulations.
Read nodal, element, global, edge, face, and set variables.
Query result variables at selected time steps.
Write or copy supported Exodus databases.
Compute simple mesh geometry quantities such as centers, volumes, and nodal volumes.
Expose JSON output for AI agents and automation tools.
common_agent_queries: python -m exodusii query mesh.exo --select n/TEMP --time last
python -m exodusii stats mesh.exo --select e/ENERGY --time last --by-block

concepts.exodus_database: An Exodus II database is a NetCDF file containing finite-element mesh topology, sets, blocks, coordinates, time values, and result variables.

entities.global: Whole-database result variables, usually one value per time step.
entities.node: Nodal result variables, one value per node per time step.
entities.element: Element result variables, usually stored by element block.
entities.edge: Edge result variables, stored by edge block when edge entities exist.
entities.face: Face result variables, stored by face block when face entities exist.
entities.element_block: A group of elements with the same element type and connectivity width.
entities.edge_block: A group of edges with the same edge topology.
entities.face_block: A group of faces with the same face topology.
entities.node_set: A set of nodes, optionally with distribution factors.
entities.side_set: A set of element-side pairs, optionally with distribution factors.
entities.edge_set: A set of edges, optionally with orientations and distribution factors.
entities.face_set: A set of faces, optionally with orientations and distribution factors.
entities.element_set: A set of elements, optionally with distribution factors.

time_indexing.python_api: Modern API time indexes are zero-based when integers are used.
time_indexing.legacy_api: Legacy ExodusIIFile-style methods usually use one-based time_step arguments.
time_indexing.cli: The agent CLI accepts first, last, index:N, step:N, or a physical float time.

connectivity_indexing.modern_api_default: Modern reader methods return one-based connectivity by default.
connectivity_indexing.zero_based_option: Many methods accept zero_based=True to return Python-friendly zero-based connectivity.

commands.summary: The agent-oriented CLI is available through python -m exodusii and prints JSON by default with indent=2. Use --terse for compact JSON.

learn.purpose: Query static exodusii capabilities and skills for self-learning.

inspect.purpose: Print an agent-friendly summary of one Exodus database.

blocks.purpose: Print element, edge, and face block metadata.

sets.purpose: Print node, side, edge, face, and element set metadata.

query.purpose: Query result variables from a database and emit JSON records.
examples: python -m exodusii query mesh.exo --select n/TEMP --time last --limit 10
python -m exodusii query mesh.exo --select e/ENERGY --time step:5 --limit 10

stats.purpose: Compute compact numeric summaries for selected variables.
examples: python -m exodusii stats mesh.exo --select n/TEMP --time last
python -m exodusii stats mesh.exo --select e/ENERGY --time last --by-block

json_format.terse: Use --terse for compact JSON with separators(',', ':').

query.summary: The database query command extracts result variables from Exodus databases. The static learn query path extracts information from installed JSON capability datasets.

special_node_selectors.n/displacements: Nodal displacement vectors when displacement variables are present.

lineouts.summary: The Lineout helper can restrict spatial tabular data to a line parallel to a coordinate axis.
lineouts.cli_status: If wired into the JSON CLI, lineout specifications should mirror exoread's -L/--lineout behavior.

python_api.summary: The modern API is centered on ExodusFile for reading, ExodusWriter for writing, and ParallelExodusFile for aggregating decomposed files.

open.example:
with ExodusFile.open('mesh.exo') as exo:
    print(exo.title)
    print(exo.dimension)

values.global: exo.values('TOTAL_ENERGY', on='global') returns a time history.
values.node: exo.values('TEMP', on='node', time='last') returns nodal values at one time.
values.element: exo.values('ENERGY', on='element', block_id=1, time='last') returns values for one block.
values.all_element_blocks: exo.values('ENERGY', on='element', time='last') concatenates block values.
values.set_variable: exo.values('VAR', on='node_set', set_id=10, time='last') reads one set variable.

parallel.example:
with ParallelExodusFile.open('mesh.e.2.0', 'mesh.e.2.1') as exo:
    coords = exo.coordinates()
    values = exo.values('TEMP', on='node', time='last')

writer.purpose: Create new Exodus databases from arrays.
writer.note: Initialize first, define coordinates/blocks/sets, define variables, then write time and values.

functions.entity_centers: Compute centers from zero-based connectivity and coordinates.

legacy.summary: The compatibility layer preserves much of the historical ExodusIIFile-style API.
legacy.time_indexing: Legacy methods generally use one-based time_step arguments.

query_cli: Large arrays are truncated by default; use --limit -1 carefully.
The JSON database query command depends on the capabilities of exodusii.api.query.
Some advanced Exodus entities may require direct Python API access if not exposed through the CLI.
static_capabilities: The static capability dataset is a compact guide, not a full API reference.
Source code and generated API documentation remain authoritative for exact signatures.
file_support: Supports common Exodus II NetCDF structures; unusual files may require additional compatibility work.
